newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar stabilises in late PM trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar stabilises in late PM trade.

text.p: White sugar futures held relatively steady during late afternoon trading after the market had been under pressure from speculative selling and liquidation earlier.
At the close August was trading at $316.60 a tonne, down $2.50 from Monday, after a day's low of $316.20.

Traders said one leading commission house had been instrumental in the earlier selling spree and was believed to have been acting for speculator clients. It had sold several thousand lots of August this week, they said.
"It's spec liquidation in the August...it's hammered the spread into the dust. There was no support at $4 but maybe at $3," said one trader.
Earlier, other traders said they expected August/October to narrow further towards support at $4.00 after commission house sales pushed it under $5.00.
Market sources said much of the August activity was being channelled towards the July raws contract in New York, where the nearby arbitrage was trading at between $72.50 and $73.00.
Technically, August has now broken initial support at $316.60 -- a consecutive series of lows from last month.
While short-term momentum indicators are in negative territory and are pointing lower, analysts noted that August's relative strength indices (RSI) have yet to indicate an oversold condition.
August's 14-day RSI is standing at 38, above the recognised 30-value oversold buffer.
But the more sensitive 9-day RSI has just slipped under the buffer to stand at 29, suggesting an upward correction could be on the cards at some stage.
Technical analysts said while a test of $315 was on the cards, uptrend support at $314.20 was still expected to hold. Resistance was pegged at $320 and $324.
In Paris volume totalled 693 lots, mostly in August which stood $0.50 lower at $316.20.
